title: Focused test runs on a many-core host don't show their test-thread count, so results aren't comparable with a gate
outcome: Anyone reading a focused run's result can see how many test threads it used, and the documentation and runner brief explain why a direct cargo test on a many-core host is harsher than a gate, without changing the default.
acceptance: A focused launcher run records the effective test-thread setting or states that libtest chose it, in its results and summary, with a test; the launcher's existing results readers still parse it

docs/test.md and the runner brief state that a direct focused cargo test skips scripts/test-rust.sh, that a test passing only at 4 threads is a finding, and that the thread count isn't set to make a failing test pass; focused runs keep their current default

completion.summary: Focused launcher runs now record the test-thread setting in results.json and print it in the summary, and docs/test.md explains why a direct cargo test on a many-core host is harsher than a gate. The default is unchanged. Landed in 91a3da13; seen on a real run on Windows B. Acceptance evaluation not requested, per Greg's rule (memory greg-acceptance-evaluation-non-blocking-2026-11-02).
